subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For Codex-backed turns interrupted by Gateway restart or app-server client close after possible side effects, should OpenClaw resume, synthesize a final status, or fail closed with restart-specific recovery guidance?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses replay safety, Codex transport failure classification, Gateway lifecycle, and channel delivery; the source has partial mechanisms but no single owner-approved policy for this combined case.

options.title: Design restart-aware recovery
options.body: Define a cross-surface policy for Gateway-shutdown interruption, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused tests.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics and copy
options.body: Keep runtime behavior fail-closed but make logs and user-facing messages distinguish Gateway restart from unexpected app-server failure.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open under live-repro follow-up until a current-main run proves the long-maintenance failure trigger and channel-delivery result.

recommendation.title: Design restart-aware recovery
recommendation.body: Define a cross-surface policy for Gateway-shutdown interruption, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Their current and historical Codex app-server retry/user-facing failure work makes them the strongest routing owner for the product boundary decision.
